researcher: claude, offline-style read of the vendor docs pages named in each fact (phase 88)

facts.claim: The Messages API lives under https://api.twilio.com/2010-04-01 (Accounts/{AccountSid}/Messages).
Fetching a message returns a single Message resource by SID; creating one is a POST to the Messages list resource.
facts.evidence: Page: 'Returns a single Message resource specified by the provided Message SID'; 'To send a new outgoing message, send an HTTP POST request to your Account's Messages list resource URI.'

facts.claim: Requests use HTTP Basic credentials: Account SID or API key SID as user, Auth Token or key secret as password.
facts.evidence: The page shows curl -u user:secret and says the Auth Token provides REST API access; it does not name the scheme in words.
All endpoint URLs on the page are on api.twilio.com.

facts.claim: A message can be deleted (a Delete a Message section exists); the exact path was not read.
facts.evidence: The page lists 'Delete messages from your account' and a 'Delete a Message resource' section; the fetch cut the text before it.

choices.decision: send and call are consent, every DELETE is consent
choices.because: they cost money, reach a person, or destroy a record; a plain POST elsewhere stays a write

choices.decision: basic auth with a secret ref

open: No live call was made. The Auth Token versus API key choice, and the delete path, are unverified.
The consent globs assume the message-send path is /Accounts/*/Messages.json (f1).
